what_its_for: Encorafenib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of melanoma (a type of skin cancer) that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery. It is also used to treat a certain type of colorectal cancer (bowel cancer) that has spread to other parts of the body. It only works in people whose cancer has a specific gene change called a BRAF V600E or V600K mutation. Your doctor will test for this mutation before starting treatment.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsules. Take encorafenib at about the same time every day. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take an extra dose — just take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. This medicine is almost always taken together with another cancer medicine called binimetinib (Mektovi) or cetuximab (Erbitux), depending on your type of cancer.
dosing: The usual dose for most adults is 450 mg (six 75 mg capsules) taken by mouth once a day when used with binimetinib for melanoma, or 300 mg (four 75 mg capsules) once a day when used with cetuximab for colorectal cancer. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it is more than 12 hours until your next scheduled dose, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is less than 12 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store encorafenib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, and starfruit, as they can increase the amount of this medicine in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen and protective clothing, as this medicine can increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL other medicines you take, including vitamins, supplements, and herbal products, because many medicines can interact with encorafenib. Do not become pregnant while taking this medicine — use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 2 weeks after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: new or worsening vision changes or eye pain; chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, or shortness of breath; unusual bleeding or bruising; signs of a new skin growth, sore, or unusual skin change; severe muscle pain or weakness; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or upper right stomach pain; severe headache, confusion, or seizures; fever or signs of infection; or any side effect that feels serious or is not getting better. Women should tell their doctor right away if they become pregnant during treatment.
when_it_works: Your doctor will monitor how well the medicine is working through regular check-ups, blood tests, and imaging scans. Some people may notice changes in their tumors within weeks, but it may take several months to know the full effect. Do not stop taking this medicine unless your doctor tells you to, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Encorafenib can harm an unborn baby. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant. Women who can become pregnant must use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 2 weeks after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use contraception during treatment and for at least 2 weeks after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 2 weeks after the last dose. Liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for mild or moderate kidney disease. Older adults (65 years and older): This medicine can be used in older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely for side effects. Pediatric patients: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been established.
